summary: This is a strong, well-structured review. It concludes the script is not safe and needs redesign. It marks missing fencing, unbounded mass-evacuation scope and local-storage data loss as blocking. It explains why a missed heartbeat does not prove the host is dead. It flags the missing dry run, logging, stop conditions, lock and idempotency. It proposes a staged path: detect and page first, then fencing, then bounded automation. It names the specific lines behind each finding. It does not commit either critical error and makes no book citations. The only faithfulness issue is small: it calls the 7-line script '9 lines'.
